passages.text: Now this was the allotment for the tribe of Manasseh as Joseph’s firstborn son, namely for Machir the firstborn of Manasseh and father of the Gileadites, who had received Gilead and Bashan because Machir was a man of war.
passages.sermon:
Manasseh was Joseph’s firstborn son.
The tribe of Manasseh received an allotment.
Machir was the firstborn son of Manasseh.
Machir was the father of the Gileadites.
Machir was a man of war.
Machir received the land of Gilead and Bashan.
passages.original: וַיְהִ֤י הַגּוֹרָל֙ לְמַטֵּ֣ה מְנַשֶּׁ֔ה כִּי־ ה֖וּא בְּכ֣וֹר יוֹסֵ֑ף לְמָכִיר֩ בְּכ֨וֹר מְנַשֶּׁ֜ה אֲבִ֣י הַגִּלְעָ֗ד כִּ֣י ה֤וּא הָיָה֙ אִ֣ישׁ מִלְחָמָ֔ה וַֽיְהִי־ ל֖וֹ הַגִּלְעָ֥ד וְהַבָּשָֽׁן׃

passages.text: So this allotment was for the rest of the descendants of Manasseh—the clans of Abiezer, Helek, Asriel, Shechem, Hepher, and Shemida. These are the other male descendants of the clans of Manasseh son of Joseph.
passages.sermon:
Manasseh was a son of Joseph.
Manasseh had several descendants.
Some descendants of Manasseh received land.
These descendants belonged to different clans.
The clans were Abiezer, Helek, Asriel, Shechem, Hepher, and Shemida.
These men were the remaining male descendants of Manasseh.
Each clan received its own share of land.
passages.original: וַ֠יְהִי לִבְנֵ֨י מְנַשֶּׁ֥ה הַנּוֹתָרִים֮ לְמִשְׁפְּחֹתָם֒ לִבְנֵ֨י אֲבִיעֶ֜זֶר וְלִבְנֵי־ חֵ֗לֶק וְלִבְנֵ֤י אַשְׂרִיאֵל֙ וְלִבְנֵי־ שֶׁ֔כֶם וְלִבְנֵי־ חֵ֖פֶר וְלִבְנֵ֣י שְׁמִידָ֑ע אֵ֠לֶּה בְּנֵ֨י מְנַשֶּׁ֧ה בֶּן־ יוֹסֵ֛ף הַזְּכָרִ֖ים לְמִשְׁפְּחֹתָֽם׃

passages.text: But Zelophehad son of Hepher (the son of Gilead, the son of Machir, the son of Manasseh) had no sons but only daughters. These are the names of his daughters: Mahlah, Noah, Hoglah, Milcah, and Tirzah.
passages.sermon:
Zelophehad was a descendant of Manasseh.
Manasseh was the son of Joseph.
Zelophehad was the son of Hepher.
Hepher was the son of Gilead.
Gilead was the son of Machir.
Machir was the son of Manasseh.
Zelophehad had no sons.
Zelophehad had only daughters.
The names of his daughters were Mahlah, Noah, Hoglah, Milcah, and Tirzah.
passages.original: וְלִצְלָפְחָד֩ בֶּן־ חֵ֨פֶר בֶּן־ גִּלְעָ֜ד בֶּן־ מָכִ֣יר בֶּן־ מְנַשֶּׁ֗ה לֹא־ הָ֥יוּ ל֛וֹ בָּנִ֖ים כִּ֣י אִם־ בָּנ֑וֹת וְאֵ֙לֶּה֙ שְׁמ֣וֹת בְּנֹתָ֔יו מַחְלָ֣ה וְנֹעָ֔ה חָגְלָ֥ה מִלְכָּ֖ה וְתִרְצָֽה׃

passages.text: They approached Eleazar the priest, Joshua son of Nun, and the leaders, and said, “The LORD commanded Moses to give us an inheritance among our brothers.” So Joshua gave them an inheritance among their father’s brothers, in keeping with the command of the LORD.
passages.sermon:
The daughters of Zelophehad came forward.
Zelophehad was a descendant of Manasseh, the son of Joseph.
These daughters stood before Eleazar the priest.
They also stood before Joshua son of Nun.
They stood before the leaders of Israel.
They said, “The LORD commanded Moses to give us an inheritance among our brothers.”
Joshua obeyed the LORD’s command.
Joshua gave them an inheritance among their father’s brothers.
passages.original: וַתִּקְרַ֡בְנָה לִפְנֵי֩ אֶלְעָזָ֨ר הַכֹּהֵ֜ן וְלִפְנֵ֣י׀ יְהוֹשֻׁ֣עַ בִּן־ נ֗וּן וְלִפְנֵ֤י הַנְּשִׂיאִים֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר יְהוָה֙ צִוָּ֣ה אֶת־ מֹשֶׁ֔ה לָֽתֶת־ לָ֥נוּ נַחֲלָ֖ה בְּת֣וֹךְ אַחֵ֑ינוּ וַיִּתֵּ֨ן לָהֶ֜ם אֶל־ פִּ֤י יְהוָה֙ נַֽחֲלָ֔ה בְּת֖וֹךְ אֲחֵ֥י אֲבִיהֶֽן׃

passages.text: Thus ten shares fell to Manasseh, in addition to the land of Gilead and Bashan beyond the Jordan, because the daughters of Manasseh received an inheritance among his sons. And the land of Gilead belonged to the rest of the sons of Manasseh.
passages.sermon:
Manasseh was a tribe of Israel.
Manasseh received ten shares of land.
These ten shares were separate from the land of Gilead and Bashan.
Gilead and Bashan were regions beyond the Jordan River.
The daughters of Manasseh received an inheritance among his sons.
Because of this, Manasseh received ten shares.
The rest of the sons of Manasseh received the land of Gilead.
passages.original: וַיִּפְּל֥וּ חַבְלֵֽי־ מְנַשֶּׁ֖ה עֲשָׂרָ֑ה לְבַ֞ד מֵאֶ֤רֶץ הַגִּלְעָד֙ וְהַבָּשָׁ֔ן אֲשֶׁ֖ר מֵעֵ֥בֶר לַיַּרְדֵּֽן׃ כִּ֚י בְּנ֣וֹת מְנַשֶּׁ֔ה נָחֲל֥וּ נַחֲלָ֖ה בְּת֣וֹךְ בָּנָ֑יו וְאֶ֙רֶץ֙ הַגִּלְעָ֔ד הָיְתָ֥ה לִבְנֵֽי־ מְנַשֶּׁ֖ה הַנּֽוֹתָרִֽים׃

passages.text: Now the border of Manasseh went from Asher to Michmethath near Shechem, then southward to include the inhabitants of En-tappuah.
passages.sermon:
Manasseh was a tribe of Israel.
The border of Manasseh started at Asher.
It went to Michmethath.
Michmethath was near Shechem.
The border then turned south.
It reached the people living in En-tappuah.
passages.original: וַיְהִ֤י גְבוּל־ מְנַשֶּׁה֙ מֵֽאָשֵׁ֔ר הַֽמִּכְמְתָ֔ת אֲשֶׁ֖ר עַל־ פְּנֵ֣י שְׁכֶ֑ם וְהָלַ֤ךְ הַגְּבוּל֙ אֶל־ הַיָּמִ֔ין אֶל־ יֹשְׁבֵ֖י עֵ֥ין תַּפּֽוּחַ׃

passages.text: The region of Tappuah belonged to Manasseh, but Tappuah itself, on the border of Manasseh, belonged to Ephraim.
passages.sermon:
Manasseh was a tribe of Israel.
The region called Tappuah belonged to Manasseh.
Tappuah was a town on the border of Manasseh’s land.
The town of Tappuah belonged to the tribe of Ephraim.
passages.original: לִמְנַשֶּׁ֕ה הָיְתָ֖ה אֶ֣רֶץ תַּפּ֑וּחַ וְתַפּ֛וּחַ אֶל־ גְּב֥וּל מְנַשֶּׁ֖ה לִבְנֵ֥י אֶפְרָֽיִם׃

passages.text: From there the border continued southward to the Brook of Kanah. There were cities belonging to Ephraim among the cities of Manasseh, but the border of Manasseh was on the north side of the brook and ended at the Sea.
passages.sermon:
Manasseh was a tribe of Israel.
The border of Manasseh continued from its previous point.
The border went southward.
It reached the Brook of Kanah.
Some cities in this area belonged to Ephraim.
These Ephraimite cities were among the cities of Manasseh.
The border of Manasseh was on the north side of the brook.
The border ended at the Sea.
passages.original: וְיָרַ֣ד הַגְּבוּל֩ נַ֨חַל קָנָ֜ה נֶ֣גְבָּה לַנַּ֗חַל עָרִ֤ים הָאֵ֙לֶּה֙ לְאֶפְרַ֔יִם בְּת֖וֹךְ עָרֵ֣י מְנַשֶּׁ֑ה וּגְב֤וּל מְנַשֶּׁה֙ מִצְּפ֣וֹן לַנַּ֔חַל וַיְהִ֥י תֹצְאֹתָ֖יו הַיָּֽמָּה׃

passages.text: Ephraim’s territory was to the south, and Manasseh’s was to the north, having the Sea as its border and adjoining Asher on the north and Issachar on the east.
passages.sermon:
Ephraim was a tribe of Israel.
Manasseh was also a tribe of Israel.
Ephraim’s land lay to the south.
Manasseh’s land lay to the north.
The Sea marked the border of their land.
Manasseh’s land touched Asher’s land on the north.
Manasseh’s land touched Issachar’s land on the east.
passages.original: נֶ֣גְבָּה לְאֶפְרַ֗יִם וְצָפ֙וֹנָה֙ לִמְנַשֶּׁ֔ה וַיְהִ֥י הַיָּ֖ם גְּבוּל֑וֹ וּבְאָשֵׁר֙ יִפְגְּע֣וּן מִצָּפ֔וֹן וּבְיִשָּׂשכָ֖ר מִמִּזְרָֽח׃

passages.text: Within Issachar and Asher, Manasseh was assigned Beth-shean, Ibleam, Dor (that is, Naphath), Endor, Taanach, and Megiddo, each with their surrounding settlements.
passages.sermon:
Manasseh was a tribe of Israel.
Manasseh received land within the territories of Issachar and Asher.
Manasseh received the city of Beth-shean.
Manasseh also received the settlements around Beth-shean.
Manasseh received the city of Ibleam.
Manasseh also received the settlements around Ibleam.
Manasseh received the city of Dor.
Dor is also called Naphath.
Manasseh also received the settlements around Dor.
Manasseh received the city of Endor.
Manasseh also received the settlements around Endor.
Manasseh received the city of Taanach.
Manasseh also received the settlements around Taanach.
Manasseh received the city of Megiddo.
Manasseh also received the settlements around Megiddo.
These cities and their settlements were part of Manasseh’s inheritance.
passages.original: וַיְהִ֨י לִמְנַשֶּׁ֜ה בְּיִשָּׂשכָ֣ר וּבְאָשֵׁ֗ר בֵּית־ שְׁאָ֣ן וּ֠בְנוֹתֶיהָ וְיִבְלְעָ֨ם וּבְנוֹתֶ֜יהָ וְֽאֶת־ יֹשְׁבֵ֧י דֹ֣אר וּבְנוֹתֶ֗יהָ וְיֹשְׁבֵ֤י עֵֽין־ דֹּר֙ וּבְנֹתֶ֔יהָ וְיֹשְׁבֵ֤י תַעְנַךְ֙ וּבְנֹתֶ֔יהָ וְיֹשְׁבֵ֥י מְגִדּ֖וֹ וּבְנוֹתֶ֑יהָ שְׁלֹ֖שֶׁת הַנָּֽפֶת׃

passages.text: But the descendants of Manasseh were unable to occupy these cities, because the Canaanites were determined to stay in this land.
passages.sermon:
The descendants of Manasseh tried to take certain cities.
They could not drive out the people living there.
The Canaanites lived in those cities.
The Canaanites refused to leave the land.
The Canaanites were determined to stay.
passages.original: וְלֹ֤א יָכְלוּ֙ בְּנֵ֣י מְנַשֶּׁ֔ה לְהוֹרִ֖ישׁ אֶת־ הֶֽעָרִ֣ים הָאֵ֑לֶּה וַיּ֙וֹאֶל֙ הַֽכְּנַעֲנִ֔י לָשֶׁ֖בֶת בָּאָ֥רֶץ הַזֹּֽאת׃

passages.text: However, when the Israelites grew stronger, they put the Canaanites to forced labor; but they failed to drive them out completely.
passages.sermon: The Israelites became strong.\r\nThey forced the Canaanites to work for them.\r\nThe Israelites did not drive out the Canaanites completely.
passages.original: וַֽיְהִ֗י כִּ֤י חָֽזְקוּ֙ בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל וַיִּתְּנ֥וּ אֶת־ הַֽכְּנַעֲנִ֖י לָמַ֑ס וְהוֹרֵ֖שׁ לֹ֥א הוֹרִישֽׁוֹ׃ס

passages.text: Then the sons of Joseph said to Joshua, “Why have you given us only one portion as an inheritance? We have many people, because the LORD has blessed us abundantly.”
passages.sermon:
The sons of Joseph spoke to Joshua.
They said, “Why did you give us only one portion as our inheritance?
We are a large people.
The LORD has blessed us greatly.”
passages.original: וַֽיְדַבְּרוּ֙ בְּנֵ֣י יוֹסֵ֔ף אֶת־ יְהוֹשֻׁ֖עַ לֵאמֹ֑ר מַדּוּעַ֩ נָתַ֨תָּה לִּ֜י נַחֲלָ֗ה גּוֹרָ֤ל אֶחָד֙ וְחֶ֣בֶל אֶחָ֔ד וַֽאֲנִ֣י עַם־ רָ֔ב עַ֥ד אֲשֶׁר־ עַד־ כֹּ֖ה בֵּֽרְכַ֥נִי יְהוָֽה׃

passages.text: Joshua answered them, “If you have so many people that the hill country of Ephraim is too small for you, go to the forest and clear for yourself an area in the land of the Perizzites and the Rephaim.”
passages.sermon:
Joshua was the leader of Israel.
The sons of Joseph spoke to Joshua.
Joshua answered them.
He said, “You have many people.”
He said, “If the hill country of Ephraim is too small for you, go to the forest.”
He said, “Clear land for yourself there.”
He said, “The forest is in the land of the Perizzites and the Rephaim.”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר אֲלֵיהֶ֜ם יְהוֹשֻׁ֗עַ אִם־ עַם־ רַ֤ב אַתָּה֙ עֲלֵ֣ה לְךָ֣ הַיַּ֔עְרָה וּבֵרֵאתָ֤ לְךָ֙ שָׁ֔ם בְּאֶ֥רֶץ הַפְּרִזִּ֖י וְהָֽרְפָאִ֑ים כִּֽי־ אָ֥ץ לְךָ֖ הַר־ אֶפְרָֽיִם׃

passages.text: “The hill country is not enough for us,” they replied, “and all the Canaanites who live in the valley have iron chariots, both in Beth-shean with its towns and in the Valley of Jezreel.”
passages.sermon:
The sons of Joseph spoke to Joshua.
They said the hill country is not enough for us.
Many Canaanites live in the valley.
All these Canaanites have iron chariots.
Canaanites live in Beth-shean and its towns.
Canaanites also live in the Valley of Jezreel.
passages.original: וַיֹּֽאמְרוּ֙ בְּנֵ֣י יוֹסֵ֔ף לֹֽא־ יִמָּ֥צֵא לָ֖נוּ הָהָ֑ר וְרֶ֣כֶב בַּרְזֶ֗ל בְּכָל־ הַֽכְּנַעֲנִי֙ הַיֹּשֵׁ֣ב בְּאֶֽרֶץ־ הָעֵ֔מֶק לַֽאֲשֶׁ֤ר בְּבֵית־ שְׁאָן֙ וּבְנוֹתֶ֔יהָ וְלַֽאֲשֶׁ֖ר בְּעֵ֥מֶק יִזְרְעֶֽאל׃

passages.text: So Joshua said to the house of Joseph—to Ephraim and Manasseh—“You have many people and great strength. You shall not have just one allotment, because the hill country will be yours as well. It is a forest; clear it, and its farthest limits will be yours. Although the Canaanites have iron chariots and although they are strong, you can drive them out.”
passages.sermon:
Joshua spoke to the house of Joseph.
The house of Joseph included Ephraim and Manasseh.
Joshua said, “You have many people.
You have great strength.
You will not have only one portion of land.
The hill country will also belong to you.
The hill country is a forest.
You must clear the forest.
The farthest parts of the hill country will be yours.
The Canaanites live there.
The Canaanites have iron chariots.
The Canaanites are strong.
You will drive out the Canaanites.”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר יְהוֹשֻׁ֙עַ֙ אֶל־ בֵּ֣ית יוֹסֵ֔ף לְאֶפְרַ֥יִם וְלִמְנַשֶּׁ֖ה לֵאמֹ֑ר עַם־ רַ֣ב אַתָּ֗ה וְכֹ֤חַ גָּדוֹל֙ לָ֔ךְ לֹֽא־ יִהְיֶ֥ה לְךָ֖ גּוֹרָ֥ל אֶחָֽד׃ כִּ֣י הַ֤ר יִֽהְיֶה־ לָּךְ֙ כִּֽי־ יַ֣עַר ה֔וּא וּבֵ֣רֵאת֔וֹ וְהָיָ֥ה לְךָ֖ תֹּֽצְאֹתָ֑יו כִּֽי־ תוֹרִ֣ישׁ אֶת־ הַֽכְּנַעֲנִ֗י כִּ֣י רֶ֤כֶב בַּרְזֶל֙ ל֔וֹ כִּ֥י חָזָ֖ק הֽוּא׃פ
